title: A drawing reads numbers from a data file
body:
Every value in an acre file is typed into the file. `let` names a value, and arithmetic works inside parentheses.

Both nail figures draw values that a program computed. These are the bounds of a cloud on each anti-diagonal, the first and last column of each matrix row, the steps of an alignment, and a grid of DP scores. To get them in, the figures were templates. A Python script substituted generated nodes for placeholders such as `@FWD@` and `@GRID_TRIM@`. The script then owned the geometry. So the `.acre` file was not the source of the figure, and `acre fmt` ran on generated output.

## Proposal

A drawing reads a TSV or CSV file by a path relative to the drawing, and names its columns. A `polygon`, a `polyline`, a `row` or a grid takes points, cells or cell text from those columns. One possible shape:

```acre
data fwd { file "fwd-cloud.tsv"; columns seq prf; }
polyline { points fwd.prf fwd.seq; }
```

## Open

- Whether a column maps through a scale into pixels, or the drawing does arithmetic on each value.
- Whether a data file may also fill a `table` or a `text`. The cloud-search figure typed 13 rows of scores into a `table` by hand.
